question: When combining Adversaries, how do you handle Escalation on Stage 3 Invader Cards when the Escalation cares about terrain? (France, Sweden)
answer:
Choose one of the two land types randomly. (JE p. 19) Don't use "top terrain" or "bottom terrain"; they not equally distributed. If there's no other convenient way, spin the card and use the terrain that's closest to pointing at the Adversary panel.
If you just apply the Escalation to both Explored terrains, Sweden's Escalation becomes much nastier and France's becomes much more lenient.

question: When combining the two Habsburg Adversaries, when does Migratory Herders (Livestock Colony Level 1) Gather check which lands match the Salt Deposits card (Mining Expedition Level 4)?
answer:
Migratory Herders checks which lands match (i.e., non-Mining lands) after the Build Step is over. Builds in the non-Mining Lands might turn them into Mining Lands before Towns are Gathered, reducing the number of lands where Migratory Herders does anything. The list of lands that will be Gathered into is fixed at this point, before any Gathers happen.
However, which lands can be gathered from, the lands that don't match (i.e., Mining lands) is checked when actually Gathering the Town, so it's possible to Gather a Town into a non-Mining land to turn that land into a Mining land, and then Gather that Town into the next non-Mining land.

question: When counting how many Invaders are in a land, are you counting pieces? Or do Towns count as 2 and Cities as 3?
answer:
You're counting pieces.
"Invader" in the Glossary is defined as "A City, Town, or Explorer", so a land with three Towns and a City has four Invaders in it. 
(A few effects instead key off of "N Health worth of Invaders", and in those cases Towns and Cities generally count for 2 and 3, respectively.)
Similarly if checking if Dahan "outnumber" Invaders, you are counting physical pieces.
tags: Favors Called Due (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When counting the number of power cards you have in play or have played (e.g., for "Draw Towards a Consuming Void"), do you count the extra Power Card from "Aid from Lesser Spirits"?
answer:
No. The card is "used as if played," but is not in play.
So with the extra card, you:
- Can use the threshold of "Draw Towards a Consuming Void" if you have no other Power Cards in play;
- Can't count the card towards extra Energy with "Boon of Vigor" or "Gift of Seismic Energy"; and
- Can't count the card towards the "Power Cards you have in play" requirements of "Earth Shudders, Buildings Fall".
tags: Boon of Vigor (River Surges in Sunlight)
Gift of Seismic Energy (Dances Up Earthquakes)
Earth Shudders, Buildings Fall (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When Dances Up Earthquakes gains Energy directly onto impending cards, is that Energy decreased by Bargains or increased by Back Against the Wall?
answer: No, those effects modify the Energy gained into a Spirit's individual Energy stockpile, not the amount gained onto impending cards.
tags: Rhythmic Power Builds to a Cataclysmic Crescendo (Dances Up Earthquakes)
Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When Dances Up Earthquakes plays a Major Power via Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power, what happens if you make that Power Card impending?
answer:
If you choose to Forget the Power at end of turn, then nothing useful happens: you make the card impending, then Forget it when the turn ends without ever using it.
If you choose to pay with Energy, "Begin a Dance of Decades" lets you pay any amount of Energy – even more than the amount you'd normally have to pay. This may be advantageous if you want reduce the time it will spend impending. The impending card will then come into play on a future turn based on the card's printed cost, like impending cards normally do. It won't automatically gain all elemental thresholds on that future turn since that effect of "Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power" expires when Time Passes this turn.

Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When Dances Up Earthquakes puts an impending card into play, can it immediately make the card impending again?
answer: No. Dances Up Earthquakes can only make a Power Card impending when it wasn't already impending.
tags: Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)
Rhythmic Power Builds to a Cataclysmic Crescendo (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When Dark Fire counts Moon as Fire (or vice versa), is that in addition to still being Moon?
answer:
No. A Moon that counts as Fire no longer counts as Moon for that action (but may count as Moon again for a future action).
Dark Fire essentially tracks only seven Elements: Sun, Darkfire, Air, Water, Earth, Plant, and Animal. As far as it's concerned, a Power in play with both Moon and Fire on it has 2 Darkfire symbols on it, and a 4 Moon 2 Fire threshold is a 6 Darkfire threshold.
tags: Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When Dark Fire gains a Moon/Fire for only a single action (e.g., when playing Elemental Invocation), can it treat that Element as the other?
answer:
Yes. That is an Element available to you, even if it's only available for a limited purpose.
This also applies in the rare case that the Dark Fire Aspect is gifted "Elemental Teachings" and spends a prepared Element marker to have an Element for a single action. But it doesn't let the Dark Fire Aspect use Moon markers as Fire markers or vice versa, whether to spend with "Elemental Teachings" or spend for the effect via the Intensify Aspect. (The Dark Fire Aspect has flexibility in the first case only because even though it spends a Moon Marker as a Moon Marker, the resulting Moon Element can instead count as a Fire Element.)
tags: Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When Disease events do damage to Dahan, is the damage reduced by Defend powers?
answer: No, since it is not the Invaders doing damage.

question: When dividing pieces evenly between multiple lands (e.g., when moving Towns in The Great River) or Energy evenly between Spirits, do you account for existing pieces in those lands / Energy of those Spirits?
answer:
No and no. "Evenly" is checked on the things to be divided, not the result after the division.
As an example, consider 4 Towns being divided evenly between a land with 0 Towns and a land with 3 Towns. Dividing 4 Towns evenly across two lands means 2 Towns for each land, for a final result of 2 Towns and 5 Towns. While a result of 3 Towns and 4 Towns gets the Town totals closer together, that requires an uneven division of the Towns—either 3 & 1 or 4 & 0, depending on which land ends up with 4 Towns.
In some cases (like The Great River), there's a tiebreaker condition if a perfectly even distribution isn't possible. In all other cases, players break ties, as usual.
tags: Exaltation of Molten Stone (Volcano Looming High)

question: When do Spirits decide whether or not to destroy Presence for the Voracious Consumption event?
answer:
When the effect triggers on that particular board after the Ravage Step.
The payment is to prevent the addition of Blight, not to prevent the creation of the "after the Ravage Step,..." triggered action when the Event Card is initially resolved.

question: When do you pay the extra Energy for Shadows of the Dahan? ("Whenever you use a Power, you may pay 1 Energy to target a land with Dahan...")
answer: When you use the Power - i.e., resolve its text effects. You don't have to choose a Power's target until you actually use it.
tags: Shadows of the Dahan (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When do you resolve a Reminder Card in the Invader Deck when accelerating multiple cards out of the deck (e.g., during the Despicable Theft scenario)?
answer:
If a Reminder Card is revealed in the middle of accelerating the deck, set it aside and then resolve it after the action that caused the acceleration (and any actions it triggered).
For Despicable Theft in particular, all Thieves in one Coastal land escape as a single action, so if multiple numbered Thieves escape from that land, accelerate the deck from all of them before resolving the revealed Reminder Card.

question: When does Blitz reduce the cost of a Fast Power and when does Blitz refund Energy for a Power being Fast?
answer:
When you play Power Cards by paying their costs {1}, total up the Energy cost of all of the Powers you’re playing and reduce it by 1 per Fast Power to determine how much you need to pay. If that number is negative, gain that much Energy as a refund.
When using a Fast Innate Power that has the potential to do something for the first time each turn, gain 1 Energy as a refund.
When you make a Slow Power Fast (via Swiftness of Lightning or similar) gain a 1 Energy rebate.
If a Fast Power Card (or a Power Card made Fast) costs 1 or more Energy, also reduce its printed cost by 1 (e.g., for Repeating it with Gift of Strength or checking when it's played by Rhythmic Power Builds to a Cataclysmic Crescendo).
{1} = This usually as part of the “Play and Pay For Power Cards” action in Spirit Phase, but sometimes a Power like Call on Midnight’s Dream tells you to do so.
tags: Gift of Strength (Vital Strength of the Earth)
Rhythmic Power Builds to a Cataclysmic Crescendo (Dances Up Earthquakes)
Dry Wood Explodes in Smoldering Splinters

question: When does Brandenburg-Prussia Level 2's early Stage III card count as Stage III and when does it count as Stage II?
answer:
It only counts as Stage II for "What Invader Stage is the game in?" (E.g., for the Second Wave Scenario, the Ward the Shores Scenario, Events, or the rules for playing with Beasts tokens but no Events.) It's still a Stage III card for anything that cares about the Stage of a specific card (e.g., the Escalation rules for Combining Two Adversaries, or Fractured Days' unique power "The Past Returns Again").
It ceases to be special once it leaves the Invader Deck (even if it returns to the deck, e.g., via "The Past Returns Again") or gets shuffled with other Stage III cards (e.g., by the Fractured Days innate power "Visions of a Shifting Future").
This is the only specially-placed Invader card that acts differently; all other cards act like their printed Stage in all circumstances.
tags: The Past Returns Again (Fractured Days Split the Sky)
Visions of a Shifting Future (Fractured Days Split the Sky)

question: When does Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine check if a piece is alone for the purpose of abducting it?
answer:
Just before resolving the sentence with the Damage/Destroy instruction.
The "+" before Damage in Power thresholds (e.g., on "Accelerated Rot") is non-functional; that's a separate Damage instruction from the one in the main Power effect.
tags: Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
Terror Stalks the Land (Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine)

question: When does destroying a Town or City cause Fear?
answer:
Always, regardless of how it's destroyed: directly via a Power that says to destroy one, from damage done by a Power, from damage done by Dahan counterattacking, due to a Spirit's special rules, from a Fear or Event card, etc. [p. 18]
Fear from destruction is independent of any explicit Fear the Power does – e.g., Lightning's "Shatter Homesteads" reads "1 Fear. Destroy 1 Town." usually generates 2 Fear: 1 explicitly, and 1 for destroying a Town.
Note that when you remove or replace a Town or City, it does NOT cause any automatic Fear. Removing Invaders happens most frequently via Fear Cards, and usually represents the Invaders fleeing, which doesn't make them any more afraid. Replacing an Invader represents some sort of transformation or change; if it's a scary change, the effect will explicitly specify how much Fear to do.

question: When does Observe the Ever-Changing World expire?
answer:
It expires when Time Passes like other effects do. The Element Markers stacked up in in the target land are a reminder of how many more times it can trigger this turn, not an actual change to the board state that persists into future turns.
All effects in Time Passes expire simultaneously, so if something else causes the pieces to change during Time Passes, Observe the Ever-Changing World does not trigger.
tags: Observe the Ever-Changing World (Shifting Memory of Ages)

question: When does Ocean's Hungry Grasp get to Drown invaders?
answer:
Apart from specific power cards, Invaders are Drowned after they are moved into the ocean on a board where Ocean's Hungry Grasp has any Presence. They do not get drowned when moved in to any other land, and Ocean's Hungry Grasp does not need to have Presence that is actually in the ocean, just on the same board.
They also do not get Drowned by any other means of Destroying the Invaders, even if it seems thematically appropriate. However an Invader is Drowned, they are Destroyed (causing Fear) and then placed on Ocean's mat for later conversion to Energy.
tags: Cast Down into the Briny Deep

question: When does Relentless Punishment check how many of your Presence are in the origin land?
answer: When you target the land with the original use of the Power, before resolving any of its effects. This most commonly matters for Focus the Sun’s Rays, but it can also matter if Presence is destroyed/removed/replaced as part of Power resolution.
tags: Focus the Sun’s Rays (Relentless Gaze of the Sun)
Relentless Punishment (Relentless Gaze of the Sun)

question: When does the damage from the 2nd level of Let Them Break Themselves Against the Stone happen?
answer:
At the same time - as part of the same triggered action - as the damage from the first level. (So, e.g., Badlands only boosts the damage once.)
It's phrased the way it is because If it also used the wording, "After Invaders deal 1 or more Damage to target land...", it would set up a separate triggered action.
tags: Let Them Break Themselves Against the Stone (Stone's Unyielding Defiance)

question: When does the Intensify Aspect spend Element Markers? Does it have to have Element Markers handy when it plays a Power during Spirit Phase?
answer:
When it's actually performing the instruction it wants to boost. In the case of Powers, this generally means when using the Power in either Fast Phase or Slow Phase. However, if a Power creates Triggered Actions, the markers are spent when the Triggered Action actually happens, which might be at a later time.
As an example, consider Infestation of Venomous Spiders. In the Fast Phase, Intensify can spend an Animal marker to add +1 Beasts and a Water marker to gather up to +1 Beasts. If it hits the threshold, it can also spend Fire each time the Damage triggers (usually in the Ravage Step, Build Step, or Explore Step) to increase that instance of Damage by 1.

question: When does the target Spirit choose when to use the Damage bonus of Gift of Furious Might?
answer:
At the moment they do Damage. They don't have to "lock in" which Power gets the bonus in advance.
This could be much later in the turn than the original Power use if the Power sets up a later condition for doing Damage (e.g., Vengeance of the Dead).
tags: Gift of Furious Might (Devouring Teeth Lurk Underfoot)

question: When doing an Invader action (Explore, Build, or Ravage), can you choose which lands they act in first?
answer:
Yes. The card tells you which lands to act in, but then the players can choose which of those lands happen first. At Invader Stage III, you can do lands of the two shown terrains in any order; you don't need to fully resolve one terrain before resolving the other terrain.
The order Explore Actions rarely matters, even if those Explores add a new source of Invaders. Similarly, the order of Build Actions rarely matters, even against Kingdom of England Level 1+.
The order does sometimes matter for Ravages, due to Blight cascades, flipping the Blight Card, or uncommon effects that change the amount of Invaders in a land that is already Ravaging, but the order won't change which lands Ravage even against Kingdom of Sweden Level 5+ or Tsardom of Russia Level 3+.

question: When Event cards ask you to discard the top major or minor power and do something on each board, do you discard just one card overall or one per board?
answer:
You discard one card for each board and follow the instructions on that board.
This affects 'Missionaries Arrive', 'New Species Spread', 'War Touches the Island's Shores', and 'Years of Little Rain'.

question: When exactly do you get the benefits from *Aid from Lesser Spirits*?
answer:
The new power card enters play as soon as the Blight card is flipped and the Spirits choose who gets which Minor Power.
You gain the elements on it immediately, and can use it for thresholds that same turn. You can also use the Power that turn, although if it is a Fast power and the Blight card flipped after the Fast phase you will not be able to use it this turn, unless something lets you use a Fast power as a Slow power.

question: When exactly do you have to pay a "cost to use" on a Power Card?
answer:
Before targeting it - "using" / "resolving" a Power includes choosing a target land and verifying that it's legal.
This can be relevant for cards like Scream Disease Into the Wind, which set up a triggered action after a Power is used on a land.

question: When exactly do you have to pay for Finder's rule Responsibilities to the Dead when you move something?
answer:
There are two cases where Finder of Paths Unseen must pay:
- When they move a piece in a way that decreases the Health of a damaged Invader/Dahan so it has now taken lethal Damage (one of many ways Finder's action can destroy the Dahan/Invaders with its own action);
- When they move an Invader/Dahan in a way that directly triggers their destruction by another action (Finder directly triggering their destruction by moving them).
The first case can happen by causing a Health penalty (e.g., Pushing a damaged Town/City into a Sacred Site of Rising Heat of Stone and Sand) or removing a Health bonus (e.g., Pushing damaged Dahan out of a land with "Infinite Vitality" or Gathering a Blight into a land with a damaged Durable Town against Habsburg Monarchy Livestock Colony Level 4).
The second case most commonly occurs in conjunction with Powers like "Melt Earth Into Quicksand" and "Call to Guard," and when teaming up with Ocean's Hungry Grasp to Push Invaders into the Ocean (but not when moving Heart of the Wildfire's Presence, since moving the Invaders/Dahan isn't what triggers "Blazing Presence").
If something prevents the destruction, then Finder does not need to pay. If one triggered action triggers another triggered action that causes destruction (like moving pieces into another Spirit's "Bargain of Coursing Paths," which then moves those pieces into another Spirit's "Melt Earth Into Quicksand"), this does not count as "directly triggering" the destruction.

Rising Heat of Stone and Sand

question: When Fathomless Mud of the Swamp uses Spreading and Dreadful Mire, does the moved Presence have to be Mud’s Presence?
answer: Yes, when one of your Actions moves Presence, it means your Presence unless otherwise specified. (This is explicitly stated in later printings of Mud.)
tags: Spreading and Dreadful Mire (Fathomless Mud of the Swamp)

question: When Fear cards say "Each player may..." do the player choices have to happen in a space where they have presence or can they affect any space on the island?
answer:
Any space on the island.
Thematically, Fear effects are what the Invaders do as a result of their rising terror. (Or, sometimes, what the Dahan do when enheartened by the Invaders' faltering resolve.) While the players make the decisions, it's not the Spirits actually taking action.

question: When Finder of Paths Unseen reveals its "+1 Range" space by placing a Presence, can it use that to extend the range at which it places that Presence?
answer: No. The Presence goes straight from the Spirit Panel to the island, there's no point at which the +1 Range is revealed but the Presence isn't already on the island.

question: When Fortune-Seekers modifies the Salt Deposits card against the Habsburg Mining Expedition, which lands match the Explore Card?
answer:
The ones without Towns/Cities.
“Non-Mining lands” is a printed land type on the Salt Deposits card, even if it’s not a standard one, so it gets replaced by the condition from Fortune-Seekers.

question: When Fractured Days Splits the Sky plays Destiny Unfolds and gains a card from their Destiny, do they also put a card in Days that Never Were?
answer: Yes, and they can usually put any card they could have picked from their Destiny into Days that Never Were; they don't have to pick a Power Card of the same type as the one they gained unless the gain effect had a restriction.
tags: Days that Never Were (Fractured Days Split the Sky)

question: When Habsburg Mining Expedition Level 1+ resolves a Build Card, when does it check which lands are Mining lands (which will Ravage instead of Build)?
answer:
When you start resolving the Build Card, determine which lands get Invader Actions and what type of Invader Actions those will be. Changing the number of Invaders in the land after that doesn't change the type of Action.
If every Invader in a Mining land doesn’t participate in Ravage, that land gets no Invader Action; if only some aren’t participating, it’ll still get a Ravage Action, since whether or not a land is a Mining land isn’t affected by participation in Ravage (or lack thereof).

question: When happens to the Deeps tokens left over by Reclaimed by the Deeps? Can they be used to sink other lands if they can somehow get moved (e.g., by Weave Together the Fabric of Place)? If they are moved, does that un-sink the land they were in?
answer:
The remaining Deeps tokens become reminder markers, which are just helpful reminders to players of which areas of the board are part of the Ocean. Reminder markers don't interact with anything on the island and don't do anything as far as the rules are concerned.
In particular, they can't be moved and aren't Deeps tokens for future uses of Reclaimed by the Deeps.

question: When Heart of the Wildfire places Presence, does it immediately get the effect of any newly-revealed Fire element?
answer:
Yes.
For instance, when you place Presence on the very first turn, you reveal one Fire icon and so get to do 1 damage after placing the Presence.

question: When I can count one piece as another, can I change that mid-action? (eg: counting Many Minds Move as One's sacred sites as a Beasts?)
answer:
Not generally, no. Unless otherwise specified, the rule for "You may count Thing X as Thing Y" is that you choose per piece, per action, and your decision applies for that whole action.
You can choose differently for nested actions - eg, if you flip the Blight card and it has immediate effects. (Example: You play Insatiable Hunger of the Swarm, and count all of your Sacred Sites as Beasts. It adds Blight which flips the Blight Card, revealing the one which destroys 1 Beasts on each board. You choose to not count any of your Sacred Sites as Beasts for that. You then continue resolving Insatiable Hunger of the Swarm, and your Sacred Sites count as Beasts for it.)
tags: A Joining of Swarms and Flocks (Many Minds Move as One)

question: When I Repeat a Major Power, if I got the threshold effect the first time, do I get it on the repetition as well?
answer:
Yes, usually.
Elements are not "used up" when you reach a threshold, so you still have the elements on the repetition. The only exception would be if you lose the elements before the repetition (e.g., you Forgot a card in play granting the elements).
tags: Gift of Strength (Vital Strength of the Earth)

question: When instructed to "Repeat this Power", do you have to obey the origin/range/target land restrictions?
answer:
Only if it doesn't tell you where to Repeat it. If a Repeat specifies where to use it, you obey those instructions, ignoring the original Range and Target restrictions (p. 19) and using the same origin land (for the rare cases where the Power's effect references that land).
For example, "The Land Thrashes in Furious Pain" could be Repeated on an adjacent land without Blight.

question: When instructed to count multiple piece types separated by slashes (e.g., "the fewest Towns/Cities"), do players choose which piece type to count?
answer: No. Count all pieces that are at least one of the types on the list. So in the example, if there are 2 Towns and 1 City in the land, the total for that land is 3 Towns/Cities. In the unlikely case that a piece is on the list multiple ways, it only gets counted once.

question: When instructed to discard a card, which cards can you choose from? Where do those cards go?
answer:
"Discard a card" without any other qualifiers means "put a Power Card from your hand into your discard pile." This most commonly occurs as part of paying for a Choice Event, but can also appear as a cost or detrimental effect.
Some effects (most notably, the standard effects of Time Passes) discard Power Cards from play because they interact with a specific card that's in play or with cards in play in general. In that case, put the Power Card(s) from play into your discard pile. You can't discard a Power Card from play unless otherwise instructed to do so.
If instructed to discard a card not controlled by a player, the card goes to that deck's discard pile. This most commonly occurs when gaining a Power Card, discarding the top card of the Event Deck on Turn 1, and when discarding a Minor Power as a randomizer.
tags: Overenthusiastic Arson (Grinning Trickster Stirs Up Trouble)
Let's See What Happens (Grinning Trickster Stirs Up Trouble)
The Border of Life and Death

question: When Invader Damage Dahan, and it is boosted by Badlands, does the boost need to be applied efficiently?
answer:
Yes.
In general, Badlands damage boosts follow the restrictions of the damage they are boosting.

question: When Invaders deal Damage to each other, is that damage dealt simultaneously?
answer:
Yes, Invaders can destroy each other this way.
Damage from a single effect is done simultaneously. For instance, with the threshold effect of Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship, a City, a Town, and 5 Explorers can wipe each other out.
For the special case involving Invaders with Strife, see here.
tags: Waters Taste of Ruin (Wounded Waters Bleeding)

question: When Invaders have increased health, does Ocean's Hungry Grasp get a bonus when exchanging them for Energy?
answer:
No. As the Special Rule says, ignore modifiers to Invader Health when trading Invaders for Energy.
This applies to all modifiers, whether permanent (e.g., England Level 5) or temporary (e.g., the Event card Tight-Knit Communities).

question: When Invaders Ravage, do they damage the land and Dahan simultaneously? Or one after the other?
answer:
Simultaneously. If they do 3 damage, they do 3 damage to the Dahan and 3 damage to the land (adding a Blight), applied at the same time.
This usually isn't relevant, but it can be if the Ravage is destroying a Presence that affects Dahan survival.
(p. 9 in 2nd printing rulebook. 1st printing incorrectly omitted "simultaneously" on p. 9, though the example on p. 11 is correct.)
tags: Earth's Vitality (Vital Strength of the Earth)

question: When is a good time to add expansion materials from Branch & Claw or Jagged Earth to the core game?
answer:
The only firm recommendation is "not right away!" - they add extra complexity while you're learning the core rules, make some core Invader dynamics more variable (and thus harder to learn), and the awesome variety they offer isn't nearly so awesome without understanding the core game. That said, some players disagree, and you should play however you like!
As a rough gauge, the more of the below questions you'd say "yes" to, the more natural it'd be to start using the expansion:
- Are you comfortable with the core game's mechanics? (No longer need to use the player aid cards / look up basic rules in the rulebook while playing, though you might consult the FAQ for edge cases. This question is the most important of the lot.)
- Have you seen much of the core game's diversity? (Played many of the Spirits / played alongside all of them; taken or considered-taking all of the Minor Powers and many of the Major Powers.)
- Are you winning games with Difficulty higher than 0? (Playing against Adversaries, or the more difficult Scenarios.)
- Have you played some of the Medium/High-complexity Spirits?
- Do you REALLY REALLY like new stuff and want to add the expansion materials as soon as possible?
- Are there more-experienced players in the game with you? (Particularly if they're already familiar with the expansion materials.)
- Are you able to predict victory more than a turn in advance? (With the only Invader randomness being the new Explore card, seasoned players can reach a point where they foresee victory multiple turns ahead of time, even when playing on a good difficulty level for them. If you've hit this point, I actively recommend breaking out the expansion, as its Event deck returns an edge of uncertainty - and thus, tension - to such situations.)
If you can say "yes" to at least 2-3 of these - definitely including the first one - then it's a fine time to add expansion materials. If you can say "yes" to 4 or more of them, no need to keep waiting! You don't need to play through literally everything in the core game's box first. (Though of course if you want to, great, do that!)
Another reasonable POV someone expressed: "Events - added in the expansion - are best when you have enough of the game system internalized that it's easy to predict what the Invaders will do. The Event Deck combats this by adding some randomness. But if you're not yet at the stage where you feel like you can picture the board 1 or 2 turns in advance, adding Events will just make it harder to do that. So waiting on the expansion until then isn't a bad idea." Though some folks like the Events more for their theme and occasional hard choices than their effects on the Invaders per se, so this may not be universal.

question: When is Swiftness of Lightning used to make Powers Fast?
answer:
During the Fast phase.
This is rarely relevant, but can matter for the Blitz Scenario: you can't "make a Power Fast" during the Spirit Phase to lower its cost by 1, only "make a Power Fast" during the Fast Phase to gain a 1-Energy rebate.

question: When is the Range bonus of Reach from the Infinite Darkness determined?
answer:
When measuring Range for a Power. Count up your Presence in The Endless Dark to determine your bonus Range at that moment.
This could be different than the amount of Presence that was in The Endless Dark when Reach from the Infinite Darkness was used earlier in the turn!

The Endless Dark (Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine)
Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine

question: When Ocean's Hungry Grasp is in play against Brandenburg-Prussia, can the extra Towns from the Stage II Escalation be placed in the Ocean (and drowned immediately)?
answer: No. The Ocean is only a land for the purpose of Powers and Blight, and not, for instance, for Events, Fear cards, or Stage II escalation effects.

question: When Ocean's Hungry Grasp is in play, can Blight, other Spirit Presence, Beasts, or other tokens end up in the Ocean?
answer:
Yes, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for many purposes, and Blight and any of the tokens from Branch & Claw can end up there. Spirit Presence from other spirits cannot be placed there during the Spirit Phase, but can end up there as a result of cards like "Indomitable Claim" or "Flow Like Water, Reach Like Air." So long as Ocean's Hungry Grasp has Presence on the board, non-human pieces in the Ocean continue to behave normally and are considered "in play" — so a Disease would count for an Event which checks if the board has Disease, for instance, even though that's an Event Action.
Invaders never take actions there, so many of the tokens will have no effect.
See also What happens to items left in the ocean if the last Presence of Ocean's Hungry Grasp is removed from the Island Board?.
tags: Gift of Proliferation (A Spread of Rampant Green)
Overgrow in a Night (A Spread of Rampant Green)
Flow Like Water, Reach Like Air

question: When Ocean's Hungry Grasps drowns a Town or a City, is the Fear earned immediately?
answer:
Yes.
The Fear is earned immediately, not when the invader piece is eventually spent for Energy.

question: When Oceans are in play, can Invader or Dahan pieces remain in the Ocean if they avoid Drowning?
answer:
No, Invaders and Dahan are not allowed to exist in the Ocean long-term. If one manages to get there without being Drowned, move them to the closest legal land after finishing resolution of whatever got them there.
In the base game, the edge-case where this can happen is if Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares uses Vengeance of the Dead (with threshold) on the Ocean itself. A Town/City/Dahan is moved to the Ocean, triggering Ocean In Play which Drowns it. Drowning (destroying) it triggers Vengeance of the Dead. If Bringer deals VotD's "damage" in an adjacent land to "destroy" a Town or Explorer and Push it into the Ocean, Ocean In Play can't trigger again, because actions can't trigger themselves, even indirectly. So the Town/Explorer isn't Drowned.
In theory it can also happen if you use Infinite Vitality (with threshold) on the Ocean then Push Dahan into the Ocean, though that's usually a pointless play.

question: When Ocean’s Hungry Grasp is on a board, can Powers and Special Rules measure Range through that board’s Ocean?
answer:
Yes, Powers and Special Rules can treat the Ocean as a land via Ocean in Play, so they can measure Range through it. Measuring Range through Land 2 is usually just as good, so this only matters if something has altered the board layout in some way:
- The Thematic Map has some Oceans that are adjacent to more than three lands.
- Land 2 is temporarily removed from play via Absolute Stasis.
- Finder of Paths Unseen is using Open the Ways to connect a land to an Ocean.
tags: Absolute Stasis (Fractured Days Split the Sky)
Open the Ways (Finder of Paths Unseen)

question: When playing a Power Card face-down in the Ward the Shores scenario, is the card still a Major/Minor/Unique Power Card for the purpose of abilities that care (e.g., the Immense Aspect)?
answer:
No, a Power Card that's played face-down loses its prior type.
To cover specific cases:
- The Immense Aspect does not gain 2 Elements for playing a Major Power face-down.
- The Intensify Aspect can't spend an Air Marker to use a face-down Minor Power during the Fast Phase.
- During the Ethereal Conjunction Event, all face-down Power Cards count as non-Major Power Cards, and can be used by that Event to add a Warding Pattern.

question: When playing against England, can A Spread of Rampant Green prevent the escalation effect or High Immigration Builds?
answer:
Yes.
Those are both Builds, so A Spread of Rampant Green's special ability Choke the Land with Green can prevent them.
England can build multiple times in the same land, and A Spread of Rampant Green would need to decide each time whether to sacrifice a Presence to prevent it.
tags: Choke the Land with Green (A Spread of Rampant Green)

question: When playing against France, if the Slave Rebellion event card causes a victory, can the next Event Card turn it into a sacrifice victory or otherwise undo it?
answer:
No. You check for victory after the Main Event ("Small Uprising" or "Rebellion") and after the Dahan Event ("Aid the Uprising"), and never get to the follow-up Event Card if you win.
Even if the 2nd Event Card is interpreted as a triggered action(†), it's not triggered by the Main Event or Dahan Event, so it doesn't need to be resolved before checking victory/defeat. (It's triggered by "finishing the Event Card", which is timing based on the game's structure similar to something like "after the Ravage Step" - not an action proper.)
(†) = And it's not clear if it should be, its wording predates "After" meaning "triggered action".

question: When playing Elemental Invocation, what happens to Element Markers on the border of lands sunk by Deeps or Destroyed by Cast Down Into the Briny Deep?
answer:
If the Element Marker is still on the border of a land, it interacts normally with Powers and other Element Markers. It still counts as being on a corner; it's just not necessarily at the intersection of multiple lands.
If the Element Marker is completely contained within a land because all lands surrounding it have been merged, then it's no longer on a land border at all and only counts towards Choice Events.
tags: Cast Down into the Briny Deep
Weave Together the Fabric of Place

question: When playing Fathomless Mud of the Swamp solo, can it gain 2 Power Cards with Exaltation of Tangled Growth?
answer: Yes. It can pay 1 Energy to gain a Power Card as “target Spirit,” and then can pay 2 Energy to gain a Power Card as “you.”
tags: Exaltation of Tangled Growth (Fathomless Mud of the Swap)

question: When playing Fractured Days Split the Sky solo, is Pour Time Sideways useless?
answer:
In a one-board game, yes, it's nearly useless. (JE p. 31) This is why you get 1 Time as compensation during Setup. Solo games are no longer strictly single-board, however, with the addition of "use an additional board" as a Play Option.
In a one-board game, Fractured Days Split the Sky is apt to want at least one Major Power if not more, so it can be useful for Forgetting.
tags: Pour Time Sideways (Fractured Days Split the Sky)

question: When playing on an Archipelago, can Many Minds Move as one Gather/Push Beasts from a coastal land on one board to a "Range 2 away" coastal land on another board?
answer: Yes.
tags: Fly Fast As Thought (Many Minds Move as One)

question: When playing on an archipelago, do two Spirits with Presence in The Endless Dark count as being on the same islet?
answer: Not unless they were already sharing an islet anyway. The Endless Dark isn't on any island board, so it's not part of any islet.
tags: The Endless Dark (Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine)
Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine

question: When playing Ward the Shores, if you play a Power Card not during the Spirit Phase, can you play it face-down to add a warding pattern?
answer: Yes, subject to the "once per turn" limit.
tags: Spur on with Words of Fire
Gift of the Primordial Deeps (Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island)
Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power
Slip the Flow of Time (Fractured Days Split the Sky)

question: When playing with against France, what happens to Towns that end up somewhere other than on the island (e.g., on the Great River panel)?
answer:
They go back into the pool of available Towns for France's loss condition, like if they were removed/destroyed. If the Towns would be used for tracking elsewhere, track that thing with another component. (e.g., swap them for 2 Explorers on the panel for Ocean's Hungry Grasp or use Scenario Markers to represent Towns that escaped in the Great River scenario.)
The intent of France's Town pool is to track how many Towns are on the island; it's just considerably easier to do this with a limited Town pool than by counting the number on the board every time one gets added. In cases where the Towns permanently leave play, it's appropriate to return them to the supply to keep that count correct, even if they'd otherwise be removed from the game entirely (e.g., by the leather sack in Powers Long Forgotten).

question: When playing with an extra board, do any Scenarios need adjusting?
answer:
Yes, a number of previously-printed Scenarios need to change "per player" to "per board":
- Powers Long Forgotten: Make the "per player" setup instructions "per board" instead. (So you have enough tokens for all the boards, if playing on balanced. )
- Blitz - Setup - "an additional Blight per player" should be "per board". Rule Changes - "1 less Blight per player" should be "per board".
- Second Wave - After the First Game - the "per player" measurements should be "per board" (though the tokens saved do not need to be exactly 1 per board - eg, in a 2p, 3-board game, you could save 3 Beasts across the whole island, not limited to precisely 1 per board). Second Game Setup - "2 Blight per player" should be "2 Blight per board".
- The Great River - Additional Loss Conditions - the per-player measurement should be per-board (but you can't just substitute "per board" because that implies it matters which board they escape from, so something like "If more than (3 x # of boards) Towns escape...")
- Ward the Shores - Setup Changes - "4 Markers per player" should be "4 Markers per board"
Note: an extra board may synergize very painfully with some Scenarios - most notably those which involve controlling / affecting territory, like The Great River, Despicable Theft, Ward the Shores and perhaps Powers Long Forgotten. If you want to avoid the extra Difficulty boost caused by this, you can opt to have some or all of the Scenario effects skip one board. (eg: The Great River could skip just Population Spills Across the River on one board, or all Rule Changes.) This will, of course, dilute the feel of the Scenario a bit.

question: When playing without Events, can you use the Stage II "Command Beasts" card during Invader Stage III?
answer:
Yes, you can use the Stage II Commanding Beasts any time after it is first unlocked.
Likewise, for an Invader that switches back and forth between Stage II and Stage III (e.g., the Tsardom of Russia at Level 4+), you can use the Stage III "Command Beasts" card anytime after you first reach Stage III.

question: When playing without Events, what type of Action is Commanding Beasts? Can you use your special rules to modify what the Beasts do?
answer:
It is a separate Event Action for each land with Beasts (JE p. 20). A Spirit's special rules generally don't apply, since they usually only affect their Powers in particular or their Spirit Actions in general.
For example, Sharp Fangs Behind the Leaves can move their Presence with the commanded Beasts, since their "Ally of the Beasts" special rule apply when Beasts move for any reason. On the other hand, Many Minds Move as One can't Push Beasts to lands 2 away, since their "Fly Fast as Thought" special rule only applies when they move the Beasts with Spirit Actions, not when Events move Beasts.

question: When Reclaimed by the Deeps sinks a land that has no adjacent lands (not even the Ocean), what happens to the Deeps tokens?
answer: Since there are no lands to Push the Deeps Tokens to, those tokens stay in place. Since they're all "remaining Deeps," they get flipped and become reminder markers.

question: When Relentless Gaze of the Sun chooses another Spirit with "Consider a Harmonious Nature," must that Spirit have Destroyed Presence?
answer:
No, Relentless Gaze of the Sun is free to choose any Spirit other than itself; the 3 Sun 1 Plant threshold just doesn’t do anything other than choosing a Spirit if the chosen Spirit has no Destroyed Presence.
The chosen Spirit can still receive Energy from the final threshold.
tags: Consider a Harmonious Nature (Relentless Gaze of the Sun)

question: When Relentless Gaze of the Sun is the only Spirit in the game, can it choose itself for the Plant thresholds of Consider a Harmonious Nature?
answer: No, the "another Spirit" exception in solo play only applies to the "Target" box, not the effects of the Power. The last two thresholds will simply fail to do anything, since choosing another Spirit is impossible.
tags: Consider a Harmonious Nature (Relentless Gaze of the Sun)

question: When Relentless Gaze of the Sun uses Consider a Harmonious Nature to destroy Presence instead of adding Blight, which Presence can it pick?
answer:
It can destroy any of its own Presence anywhere on the island, which includes Presence in The Endless Dark.
Gaze can't destroy Presence that's not on the island, including:
- On its Presence Tracks
- Removed from the game, e.g., by a Bargain
- Under the effects of Absolute Stasis
- On Serpent's Deep Slumber Track
tags: Absolute Stasis (Fractured Days Split the Sky)
Deep Slumber (Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island)

question: When Relentless Gaze of the Sun uses its final Growth option, does it also double the Elements it gains from its top Presence Track?
answer: No. That Growth option only doubles Energy gained, not all benefits from the Energy/turn track.

question: When Relentless Gaze of the Sun uses its Growth Action to move up to 3 Presence, must those Presence come from the same land?
answer:
Yes.
"Move X Together" means "X must be together for the entire movement," not "X must move in a way that they are all together at the end of the movement."

question: When Repeating a Power that has choices, do you have to make the same choice the second time?
answer:
No, when Repeating a Power, you can make different choices unless the Power explicitly says otherwise. This can include:
- Choosing a different target
- Choosing a different mode (e.g., gaining Energy with the first use of Gift of Searing Heat and then spending it with the second use)
- Choosing not to pay for something you paid for the first time (e.g., not paying for a card with the second use of Exaltation of Tangled Growth)
tags: Gift of Searing Heat (Rising Heat of Stone and Sand)
Exaltation of Tangled Growth (Fathomless Mud of the Swap)

question: When replacing a Power Card with Visions Out of Time, what happens to the 3 unchosen Power Cards?
answer: They are discarded to that deck's discard pile.

question: When resolving a 2nd (or 3rd!) Explore Card in a single Invader Phase, what's the Invader Stage while resolving the later card(s)?
answer:
Whatever if would be if they were on top of the deck (usually the Phase printed on them).
Most of the time, this distinction doesn't matter – almost all checks of the Invader Stage happen earlier in the Invader Phase, when resolving an Event Card. However, when resolving an Explore Card during the "Ward the Shores" Scenario, the Stage of the game determines which pieces are added by Explore Actions. This can change in the middle of the Explore Step when resolving multiple Explore Cards.

question: When Rising Heat of Stone and Sand has exactly two Presence in a land with a Durable Habsburg Monarchy (Livestock Colony) Town that has taken one Damage, what happens with Blight is added to the land?
answer:
The Town is destroyed.
To lay out the steps in detail:
- Heat has two Presence. The Town has 1 Damage and 3 Health.
- Blight is added. The Town has 1 Damage and 1 Health.
- Destroy one Presence (Blight was added) and the Town (it took Damage equal to or greater than its Health).
tags: Blistering Heat (Rising Heat of Stone and Sand)
Rising Heat of Stone and Sand

question: When Roiling Waters Bleeding adds a non-Beasts piece that counts as a Beasts token (e.g., the Presence of a Spirit under "Settle Into Hunting-Grounds"), does it deal Damage?
answer:
Generally, no. "Lands of Blood and Savagery" checks if the piece that's being added is already a Beasts, not if it will be a Beasts once it arrives.
Nevertheless, Roiling Waters Bleeding deals Damage if repositioning a piece on the island that already counts as a Beasts, whether that's the Incarna of Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine, the Presence of a Spirit under "Settle Into Hunting Grounds", or a Sacred Site belonging to Many Minds Move as One.
tags: A Joining of Swarms and Flocks (Many Minds Move as One)
Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
Terror Stalks the Land (Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine)

question: When Scotland Explores into Coastal Lands, what happens if there's an Isolated Coastal land? Do the other 2 Coastal lands on that board both have to add 1 Town, or can one get an Explorer?
answer:
Both non-Isolated Coastal lands get 1 Town. (And the Isolated land isn't explored.)
This happens whenever one of the Explores is prevented for whatever reason.

question: When selecting a land with Mantle of Dread, do I have to choose a land with an Explorer and a Town if I can?
answer: No. The intent of the power is that the target Spirit may select one of their lands with only an Explorer or only a Town, even if they have another land with both Explorers and Towns.
tags: Mantle of Dread (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When selecting Power Cards for Ethereal Conjunction, can you choose a Power Card made impending by Dances Up Earthquakes?
answer:
Yes.
The list of places on Ethereal Conjunction that you can choose Power Cards from is a reminder of where your Power Cards will usually be, not the complete list. Impending Cards are still Dances' Power Cards, so they can be chosen for this Event.
tags: Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When setting up a Spirit, what happens if the setup instructions are impossible (e.g., adding Presence to a land with Blight when that board has no Blight).
answer:
Either don't start that Spirit on that board or follow the instructions as best as you can, choosing freely when no lands meet the criteria given. [Jagged Earth Rulebook p. 6]
When choosing freely, use theme as your guide — if you're in this situation, you're likely playing on the thematic map, after all!
tags: Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
Unconstrained Aspect (Sharp Fangs Behind the Leaves)

question: When setting up for the later rounds in Second Wave, should you place the initial Beasts and Disease on each board?
answer:
No.
The only Tokens at the start of the game should be one of each type per player from the previous wave.

question: When something lets Dances Up Earthquakes play a Power Card during the Fast, Invader, or Slow Phases, can they make that Power Card impending?
answer: Yes, and they may pay any amount of Energy when doing so, like when making a card impending during the Spirit Phase. They don't need to pay the full Energy required by that effect (usually the cost of the card).
tags: Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When Stone's Unyielding Defiance places a Presence from a +1 Card Play space and gains a Minor Power, can you look at the new Power before deciding where to place a Presence?
answer:
No. There's no point in time when you have added the Presence but it's not already on the board.
The intent is that this is a triggered action (which makes the timing more obvious) but the special rule would be clearer if it started with "After...".
tags: Deep Layers Exposed to the Surface (Stone's Unyielding Defiance)

question: When the Blight card is flipped to the Blighted Island side, how much Blight gets added?
answer:
If the new side says N Blight per player, you add N Blight per player more. The total amount of Blight on both sides will then be N+2 Blight per player, plus one Blight more (following this erratum).
The amount of Blight on the base board is roughly balanced with the Blight cards - your total Blight pool is smaller, but you have no negative effect. However, it is slightly easier to play with - first, because the certainty of knowing exactly what will happen makes some decisions easier / clearer / less risky; second, because with ongoing-effect Blight cards, there's an early-game pressure to not let the island go Blighted (as the earlier it happens, the worse it is), whereas with the base blight space it doesn't matter when Blight is placed, only whether it empties.
(The early-game pressure is also present with immediate-effect Blight cards and the Event deck from Branch & Claw, as some Events key off the island being Blighted.)

question: When the Dark Fire Aspect discards a card with both Moon and Fire to pay for a choice event, how much Energy does that count towards the cost? How about if it forgets the power card isntead?
answer: 2 Energy and 4 Energy, respectively. The discard and forget options for Choice Events check if a card has a relevant Element, not how many of that Element is on the card.
tags: Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When the Dark Fire Aspect is playing a Scenario that cares about the Elements of cards you own, can it count Fire as Moon and vice versa?
answer: Yes. Though the Aspect only explicitly refers to Elements in play and to choice Events, it's also intended to work with scenarios like Rituals of the Destroying Flame and Elemental Invocation.
tags: Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When the Habsburg Monarchy (Livestock Colony) Level 2+ would Build a City in an Inland Fathomless Mud Sacred Site, how many Explorers get Built?
answer:
One or two Explorers, your choice.
If you choose to apply Offer No Firm Foundations first, it switches the Build from a City to an Explorer, so More Rural Than Urban doesn’t apply. On the other hand, if you choose to apply More Rural Than Urban first, it switches the Build from a City to two Towns, which Offer No Firm Foundations then switches to two Explorers.
tags: Offer No Firm Foundations (Fathomless Mud of the Swamp)

question: When the Immense Aspect would grant an extra Element at the end of the Spirit Phase, do its Plays count as 1 Play or half a Play?
answer:
1 Play. Immense has just as many Plays as Lightning's Swift Strike normally does; it just has to spend twice as many of them to play a card at the end of the Spirit Phase.
The extra Element lets Immense still get a benefit from advancing to having an odd number of plays, despite the 3rd and 5th plays not actually allowing Immense to play any more Power Cards.

question: When the Intensify Aspect spends a Moon Marker when replacing a piece of type A with a piece of type B (e.g., replacing 1 Explorer with 1 Dahan with Call of the Dahan Ways), how many piece of type B will there be?
answer: One per piece of type A that was replaced. So in this case, if there were two Explorers present, there would then be two Dahan.
tags: Gift of the Untamed Wild (Lure of the Deep Wilderness)
Crops Wither and Fade (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)
Ravaged Undergrowth Slithers Back to Life

question: When the Intensify Aspect uses a Plant marker to increase the amount of destroyed Presence added with an action, can it only add one extra instead of two extra?
answer: Only if there's exactly one extra destroyed Presence to add. If there are two extra destroyed Presence, both must be added, even if you'd rather leave one of them destroyed.

question: When the Invaders do an extra set of actions during Setup in the Blitz Scenario, does that include any Adversary effects that happen during or trigger after the Build/Explore Step?
answer:
No, while the Invaders are resolving a Build Card and two Explore Cards, they are doing so during Setup, not during the Build Step or Explore Step (which are part of the Invader Phase).
In particular, the following effects don't apply during Blitz setup because they reference specific steps of the Invader Phase or explicitly exclude setup.
- "Frontier Explorers" (The Kingdom of France Plantation Colony Level 1) and "Trading Port" (The Kingdom of Scotland Level 1) don't change which pieces are added during or after Exploring – not even from the second Explore Card – because they don't apply during setup.
- "Migratory Herders" (The Habsburg Monarchy Livestock Colony Level 1) doesn't gather Towns.
- "More Rural Than Urban" (The Habsburg Monarchy Livestock Colony Level 2) doesn't build 2 Towns in place of building an Inland City, since play hasn't started yet.
- "Ceaseless Mining" (Habsburg Mining Expedition Level 1) doesn't cause Ravage Actions in Mining lands.
- "Mining Boom" (Habsburg Mining Expedition Levels 3 & 5) doesn't upgrade or build anything.
... but these effects do happen during setup:
- "Slave Labor" (The Kingdom of France Plantation Colony Level 2) does upgrade Explorers after Building in lands with 2+ Explorers.
- "Persistent Explorers" (The Kingdom of France Plantation Colony Level 6) does add an Explorer after each of the two Explore Cards.
- "The Empire Ascendant" (Habsburg Mining Expedition Level 6) does add extra Explorers (and stack with the extra Explorer from Blitz!), since it explicitly applies during Setup.
... and these effects can happen during setup, but are unlikely to do so:
- "Triangle Trade" (The Kingdom of France Plantation Colony Level 4) does add a Town as part of Building a Coastal City, though this only happens if the first Explore Card matches a land with a Coastal Town.
- "Indentured Servants Earn Land" (The Kingdom of England Level 1) and "Chart the Coastline" (The Kingdom of Scotland Level 3) both allow building in lands without Invaders, albeit in a way that's unlikely to matter unless the first Invader Card matches a land that has a Wilds in it during Setup.

question: When the Kingdom of Sweden reveals an Escalation symbol, does the Escalation apply to all subsequent Explore Cards that turn?
answer:
No, "Swayed by the Invaders" only applies to the card with the Escalation symbol, and not to any other Explore Cards.
This also means that if the Escalation would happen when the card isn't an Explore Card (e.g., when combining with the Tsardom of Russia's "Entrench in the Face of Fear"), then the Escalation does nothing.

question: When the Mentor Aspect is the target of Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power, what happens?
answer:
Shifting Memory of Ages draws two Major Powers, gains them both, and forgets nothing. If they meet the threshold requirements, they can play one of the new Power Cards – since the identity of "the Major Power" is ambiguous, Shifting Memory of Ages chooses which one is being referred to.
It doesn't matter who played the Power, just that Shifting Memory of Ages with the Mentor Aspect is the target.
tags: Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power
Gift of the Primordial Deeps (Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island)

question: When the Mentor Aspect plays in the Destiny Unfolds scenario, do they gain two cards from its Destiny when they gain a Power Card?
answer:
Yes, if there are at least two cards left. In the unlikely case that there's exactly one card left, they just gain that one.
They are free to mix and match between Majors and Minors, though gaining two Majors at once has the benefit that they need to Forget a Power Card fewer times over the course of the game.

question: When the Nourishing Aspect gains an extra Minor Power because it gained a Major Power, can it Forget the new Minor Power?
answer: No. Completely resolve the action that gained the Major Power, including Forgetting, before gaining the Minor Power.
tags: Nourishing Aspect (Vital Strength of the Earth)

question: When the players collectively perform the Ritual of Terror, whose Action is it?
answer:
Rituals that are not explicitly associated with one Spirit are Spirit Actions for the purpose of anything that cares what type of Action they are (e.g., Vengeance as a Burning Plague destroying its Presence as part of a Ritual of Terror), but are not an individual Spirit's Action for the purpose of their Special Rules. (No, not even in solo play, for the sake of consistency.)
In Rituals of the Destroying Flame, it is an individual Spirit doing the Action, and so is that Spirit's Action and can benefit from special rules that apply to their actions.
tags: Lingering Pestilence (Vengeance as a Burning Plague)

question: When the Ravage Card is Salt Deposits, does "Farmers Seek the Dahan for Aid" cause it to Build in Mining lands, Ravage in Mining lands, or Build in non-Mining lands?
answer:
Build in Mining lands.
Which lands the Salt Deposits card matches is determined by the space it’s in on the Invader Board, so it always matches Mining lands in the Ravage space. "Farmers Seek the Dahan for Aid" then turns the Salt Deposits card into a Build Card. Since "Ceaseless Mining" only affects the Build Step, Invaders thus only Build during this rather unusual Ravage Step.
tags: Farmers Seek the Dahan for Aid

question: When the Warrior Aspect deals Damage by Dahan bringing its Incarna, can it deal the Damage before the move?
answer:
No, the Damage must be in the destination land. The Incarna hasn't been brought until it arrives in a land.
However, if one Power results in the Incarna being brought along multiple times (e.g., Gather the Warriors moving Dahan twice), the Incarna can deal Damage in any one of the lands it arrives in, even if that land is not its ultimate destination.

question: When Towns are Durable (have extra Health) due to Habsburg Monarchy (Livestock Colony) Level 4+: If Invaders blight a land during Ravage, does their Towns' extra Health wear off immediately?
answer: Yes, it drops to normal at the same time as the Blight is added / the Dahan are damaged. If any such Towns have already taken 2+ Damage, they will be destroyed immediately, before Dahan counterattack.

question: When using "Gift of Twinned Days," what happens if it's your lowest-cost Power Card in play?
answer:
If you have multiple Power Cards in play that cost 1 Energy, you can break the tie for "lowest" in favor of one of the other Power Cards in order to repeat that one.
If all of your other Power Cards cost 2 or more Energy, then the only Power Card you can repeat is "Gift of Twinned Days." You should generally decline to repeat it in that case, since repeating it does nothing.
Because "lowest-cost" is checked when actually using the repeat, you can occasionally get around "Gift of Twinned Days" being the unambiguously lowest-cost card in play by either getting it out of play or by playing an equally-cheap or cheaper Power Card.

question: When using *Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power*, can target Spirit voluntarily choose to Forget when gaining a Major Power?
answer: Yes, target Spirit is merely given the option not to Forget, not a requirement to take advantage of that benefit. That being said, Forgetting anyway is almost never beneficial.
tags: Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power

question: When using a land-targeting Power with Range "—," which land is the origin land?
answer:
In the rather rare case that it matters, you can choose any land with your Presence to be the origin of the Power.
If you don't have any Presence to use as the origin (e.g., because all of your Presence is under Absolute Stasis or in the Endless Dark), you can't use the Power.

question: When using a Power Card via Ethereal Conjunction, can you hit its thresholds? Do its own Elements contribute to those thresholds?
answer:
Yes and yes. You can use any Elements you have when you use the Minor/Unique Power, including the Elements on the Power Card itself.
However, the Power Card will be Forgotten before you have a chance to use any Powers in Slow Phase, so it won’t help you hit the Elemental thresholds of those Slow Powers.

question: When using Dances Up Earthquakes' third growth option, can you pick the same impending card twice? Can you gain extra Energy onto one impending card and less Energy onto another impending card?
answer: No and yes, respectively. You first choose which 0-2 cards you're going to affect and then separately decide which of the chosen cards (if any) will gain +1 Energy and which (if any) will gain -1 Energy when you gain Energy later that Spirit Phase.
tags: Rhythmic Power Builds to a Cataclysmic Crescendo (Dances Up Earthquakes)
Begin a Dance of Decades (Dances Up Earthquakes)

question: When using Relentless Punishment to repeat a Power Card, what counts as a previous use?
tags: Relentless Punishment (Relentless Gaze of the Sun)

question: When using Spreading and Dreadful Mire, does it matter if you don't have a Sacred Site in the origin land when you resolve the first threshold (e.g., because you targeted via Entwined Power)?
answer:
No, "the origin sacred site" is just land you picked as the origin back when targeting the Power. There isn't a second check for if that land is still your sacred site.
This only matters if you still have Presence in that land (e.g., because you and the Spirit you're entwined with each had exactly 1 Presence there); if none of the Presence there is yours, there is no Presence you can move.
tags: Spreading and Dreadful Mire (Fathomless Mud of the Swamp)

question: When using the threshold of Plague Ships Sail to Distant Ports, must Energy be spent to add the final Disease?
answer: No, the energy cost is only to remove the top card of the Fear Deck from the game. It's possible to resolve the threshold as just "1 Fear. 3 Damage. Add 1 Disease." if you don't want to pay.
tags: Plague Ships Sail to Distant Ports

question: When using Transformative Sacrifice with threshold, what's the maximum number of Minor Powers that Target Spirit can Take and Play?
answer:
Four: three from the base effect and one from the threshold.
The Presence removed from the Presence track doesn't double-count.

question: When Volcano Looming High uses Explosive Eruption vs Tsardom of Russia Level 2+, can they Push 1 Explorer from the origin land (when it does damage by destroying Presence) then destroy that Explorer using the thresholds of the innate that deal damage to nearby lands? Does that Push the Explorer again?
answer:
No, and no. Actions can't destroy Invaders that were saved from destruction earlier in that same action, so the runaway Explorer is safe. And all the damage is part of a single action, so you only Push them (and generate Fear) once.
The damage from destroying your Presence is part of the same action because the Special Rule says "When you destroy your Presence..." – it modifies how other actions work while they're happening.

question: When Volcano uses Explosive Eruption, it deals damage both via destroying its Presence and the Innate Power. Does Badlands apply twice?
answer:
No, because the damage from destroying its Presence isn't a separate action.
The Special Rule says, "When your Presence is destroyed...", which means the damage is done as part of whatever action destroyed your Presence.
(If it were instead a triggered action, it would say "After your Presence is destroyed".)
tags: Collapse in a Blast of Lava and Steam (Volcano Looming High)

question: When War Touches the Island’s Shores does Damage in a land where Rising Heat of Stone and Sand has exactly 2 Presence, can you take advantage of the Health penalty from Blistering Heat to Destroy Invaders?
answer:
Yes. There is no point at which Rising Heat's Presence has already been destroyed by the Blight, but Invaders haven't yet been checked for taking enough Damage to destroy them.
This also applies to Far-Off Wars Touch the Island against Durable Invaders.
tags: Blistering Heat (Rising Heat of Stone and Sand)
Rising Heat of Stone and Sand

question: When Weave Together the Fabric of Place expires, what if pieces in the joined land can't be legally moved to one (or both) of the printed lands?
answer:
If a piece can moved legally, it must be. If it can't be legally moved to any of the constituent lands, then it is cleaned up to one of them (player's choice which). This applies to all pieces, not just Invaders/Dahan.
(Cleaning up is not an action, not considered a move, and does not trigger actions; it is a correction of the game state.)
This can happen with, e.g., Presence placed in a normally-illegal location via Indomitable Claim.
In the ridiculously rare edge case of two Woven lands which are both no longer lands, when Weave expires, clean up all Woven pieces as if they were illegally placed in one of the used-to-be-lands. (This may require judgment calls.) If this ever arises naturally, you win an edge-case award.
tags: Weave Together the Fabric of Place

question: When Wounded Waters Bleeding claims a Healing Card, does it go to their hand?
answer: No, it goes straight to the Spirit Panel, as though you added an Aspect in the middle of the game.
tags: Seeking a Path Towards Healing (Wounded Waters Bleeding)

question: When you "Remove 3 Health worth of Invaders," can you Remove 3 damaged Towns?
answer:
No, the Health of an Invader doesn't change when it takes Damage. Damaged Towns still count for 2 Health each.
A few effects (e.g., Kingdom of England Level 5, or some Event/Fear cards) modify Health, which does affect how many Invaders you can Remove. But Damage does not reduce Health. (Health is simply the total amount of Damage it takes to destroy something.)
tags: Radiant and Hallowed Grove (Towering Roots of the Jungle)
Blistering Heat (Rising Heat of Stone and Sand)
Rising Heat of Stone and Sand

question: When you add Fear to the Fear pool mid-game, what exactly happens?
answer: You add the specified number of Fear markers from the box to the top part of the Fear Pool. They behave as normal, so for the rest of the game, it takes more Fear to earn each Fear Card.
tags: Invaders Find the Land to Their Liking

question: When you gain a new Major Power, which Power Cards can you forget?
answer: You can Forget any power card: in your hand, in your discard, or in play. You can even Forget the Major Power you just gained (sidebar, p. 18).

question: When you get the threshold on Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power, can you choose **not** to use the elemental threshold on the Power you gain?
answer:
No.
You must follow the instructions as written as best you can if you choose to activate the Unlock the Gates threshold.
tags: Unlock the Gates of Deepest Power

question: When you hit the threshold of a Major Power, is the effect in addition to the base effect?
answer: Yes, unless the card says "instead", threshold effects are in addition to the base effect [p. 17].

Vanish Softly Away, Forgotten by All

question: When you reposition Presence on the board rather than adding new Presence, where can you measure the range from?
answer:
You can measure the range from any Presence, including the one you are about to reposition.
The sequence of events for adding Presence during growth, you
- Choose a land to add Presence to. This must be measured from your Presence on the board at that moment.
- Add a Presence to that land.
Normally this is picked up from your Presence track, but you can pick it up from anywhere on the island instead if you want. The sequence is similar when a Power lets you add Presence.
tags: Gift of Proliferation (A Spread of Rampant Green)
Overgrow in a Night (A Spread of Rampant Green)

question: When you resolve a Choice Event, do you have to resolve one of the two options?
answer: Yes.

question: When you resolve a Fear card, do you resolve only the current level?
answer:
Yes, you only resolve the effect corresponding to the current Terror Level, not any previous levels. (p. 9)
You resolve it at the current Terror Level, regardless of whether the Terror Level was lower when the card was earned.

question: When you return an Invader or Fear card to the box, can you look at it?
answer: No.

question: When you return Presence to your tracks, can you cover one of the leftmost solid-circle spaces that start the game without Presence?
answer:
No, the leftmost spaces with solid circles cannot be covered by Presence.
Similarly, "Bonus" spaces (which have a solid circles and start uncovered) can never be covered. However, if a normal space with a dashed circle starts the game uncovered (e.g., in the Guard the Isle's Heart Scenario), that space can be covered.
In the rare case that this means it's impossible to return a Presence to your Presence Tracks, the returned Presence is instead destroyed. [JE p. 28]
tags: Locus Aspect (Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island)
Fragments of Shattered Time (Fractured Days Split the Sky)
Powered by the Furnace of the Earth (Volcano Looming High)
Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: When you use a Power outside of its normal phase (e.g., during the Invader Phase via the Rouse the Spirits event), if Repeats have been granted to you (e.g., from Gift of Strength), can you use them then?
answer:
Changed answer: Not to use the Power twice at that time. Unlike "Lightning's Boon" or "Sky Stretches to Shore," you're not actually changing the Power's speed, you're just using it (once) ignoring speed. Repeating a Power lets you use it again in the phase matching the Power's actual speed.
The first-pass answer was "yes" based on the idea that these things changed the Power's speed, but that proved the wrong direction.
In the uncommon case where the only reason you can't use the Power at the unusual time is having used it already, you can use a granted Repeat at that unusual time to get around the 1/turn restriction on using Powers.
Note that this only applies when granted the option to Repeat a Power later in the turn, like with "Gift of Strength" or "Powerstorm." It does not apply to Powers that have "Repeat this Power" as one of their instructions; those can and must be Repeated immediately as an action triggered by the initial use (after any other triggered actions). Similarly, if using a Power triggers the option to Repeat it immediately (rather than later in the turn), you may do so.
tags: Gift of Strength (Vital Strength of the Earth)
Gift of Abundance (Downpour Drenches the World)
Slip the Flow of Time (Fractured Days Split the Sky)

question: When your Presence track gives you "Any" element, when do you have to choose what element that is? Can you change what it is during the turn?
answer:
You can wait until the middle of your turn to choose what it is, but once you've set it for a turn, it can't change that turn [base rulebook p. 14, last item under Presence Tracks]
This holds true even if you're restricted on which Elements you can choose (e.g., Wounded Waters Bleeding having a "Water / Animal" space instead of a full "Any"). [Nature Incarnate rulebook p. 9]
This contrasts with the timing of choosing flexible Elements gained from different sources.
tags: Dark Fire Aspect (Shadows Flicker Like Flame)

question: Where is Range in the text of a Spirit-targeting Power measured from?
answer:
From the presence of the Spirit following the instruction (usually target Spirit) unless the Power explicitly says otherwise. Use the Range bonuses (if any) of the Spirit using the Power, which may not be the Spirit measuring Range.
To cover specific cases:
- For "Serpent Wakes in Power," each Spirit adds Presence within Range 1 of itself.
- "Blazing Renewal" explicitly measures Range from the Spirit using the Power, even if they're not the one adding Presence.
Contrast with land-targeting Powers, where Range arrows in the Power's effect are measured from target land

question: Which Blight is counted by "Irreparable Damage," The Habsburg Monarchy (Livestock Colony) loss condition?
tags: Hold the Island Fast with a Bulwark of Will (Stone's Unyielding Defiance)

question: Which elements does Elemental Boon have for the purpose of Events?
answer:
It is your choice (Branch & Claw rulebook, p. 16).
This is true whether you are discarding the power as a randomizer, or discarding/forgetting it to get +2/+4 Energy for Choice Events.

question: Which lands are affected by the Level 1 effect "Indentured Servants Earn Land" of the Kingdom of England?
answer:
The lands you'd normally check for Build. (Those of the Terrain type(s) showing on the Invader Card under Build.)
The only change to how Build works is that a land without Invaders might Build (if it meets the listed requirements), which normally is not the case.

question: Whose Presence does the range in Unrelenting Growth target from?
answer: It measures range from the target Spirit, since it's part of instructions telling the target what to do.

question: Why do some of the Power cards have colored corners?
answer: These are the cards that match the Power Progression Cards for the starting Spirits. You may ignore them after your first games.

question: Why does Burn Brighted Before the End have the option to remove Presence instead of adding Presence? Isn't adding Presence always better?
answer: In most instances, yes, adding Presence will be better. However, Heart of the Wildfire is often in a position where adding Presence to one of its lands will not only add more Blight, but also cascade – rather punishing for a Blighted Island card with so little Blight. Hence, there's an option to remove Presence from tracks instead.

question: Why is there a copy of Sea Monsters in Jagged Earth *and* in Branch & Claw? What's the difference?
answer:
The copy of Sea Monsters in Jagged Earth replaces the original version in Branch & Claw. It limits the maximum amount of Fear generated, to avoid ridiculous combos with Many Minds Move as One. The new text reads: "Add 1 [Beasts]. If Invaders are present, 2 [Fear] per [Beasts] (max. 8 [Fear]). 3 Damage per [Beasts]. 1 Damage per [Blight]. -If you have- 3 Water, 3 Animal: Repeat this power." If you have just Branch & Claw, you are welcome to use this new wording if you like, but it's not required.
If you have Jagged Earth but not Branch & Claw, technically, you shouldn't add Sea Monsters to the Major Power deck. But it's not a huge deal if you do - the elemental balance of the Major Power deck isn't as tightly tuned as that of the Minor Powers.

question: Will there ever be a Second Edition of Spirit Island? Or some sort of balance-tweak expansion for the current edition?
answer: Nothing is certain, but see Thoughts around the topic of Spirit Island 2nd edition.

question: With an Archipelago, can Entwined Power's 'target via each others Presence' let you avoid paying 1 Energy to target a Spirit you don't otherwise share an islet with?
answer: Yes. The check for "Do you share an islet with the Spirit you're targeting?" (and 1-Energy cost if not) is part of targeting the Power.
tags: Locus Aspect (Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island)

question: With Entwined Power, can Shroud of Silent Mist Gather another Spirit's Presence?
answer:
Yes. When Shroud of Silent Mist targets a Power (which its Presence-Gather is part of) it treats the other Spirit's Presence as also being its Presence.
If the effects of the special rule didn't have anything to do with targeting the Power, it might be more ambiguous (since Entwined Power is only supposed to affect targeting), but Mists Shift and Flow is very explicit that it can be used to target Powers.
